description: Hatsu's two harness hooks. `Stop` rings the bell — an OS notification and a sound — when a gate stop is waiting, reading the marker the jutaisho skill drops at .nen/last-stop.json; `PreToolUse` on Bash refuses a `git commit` or a `git push` while the working copy sits on the workflow base branch. NEITHER IS A NEN-OWNED STEP. They are Claude Code hooks, executed by the harness around a session rather than by a skill inside one, and they exist because a notification and a reflex refusal are the two things a skill cannot do: a skill only runs when the model calls it, and by the time the model has stopped talking or has already typed the push, it is too late. Every deterministic step the skills themselves take stays a nen verb. Both scripts are POSIX sh, use no jq, yq or python (README, 'On the installed plugin path'), and fail open — a hook that cannot read what it needs stays out of the way rather than blocking a session on its own uncertainty. The guard is the deliberate exception, and it PARSES the command rather than matching a substring: a `sh -c '<script>'` wrapper is unwrapped, quoted spans are masked, the payload's `\n`, `\t` and `\\` escapes become real characters so that a `cd` on its own line moves the directory the lines under it write in, a heredoc BODY is masked as the data it is unless the opener hands it to a shell — decided by parsing the line's command positions and comparing each first token by basename, so `/usr/bin/sh <<EOF` and `cat <<EOF | sh` RUN their body while `cat sh <<EOF` does not, and an unidentifiable consumer fails closed — the command is split into segments, and a segment counts only when its first token is `git` and the token after git's own global options (`-C`, `-c`, `--no-pager`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--namespace`, in both the separate-argument and `--key=value` forms) is `commit` or `push` — so `echo 'git commit'`, a markdown table quoting `git push -u origin HEAD` inside a heredoc, and `git commit-tree` all pass while `git -C <dir> commit` and `git --git-dir=<dir>/.git commit` are judged in <dir>. THE DIRECTORY GIT TARGETS IS THE DIRECTORY JUDGED: every `-C` the segment carries is applied cumulatively the way git applies it, `--git-dir` and `--work-tree` are resolved against the result, and only a segment carrying none of them is judged in the session's working directory; the branch.base it is compared against is read from the checkout that branch came from, which for a bare `--git-dir` aimed at a linked worktree is that worktree's own nen/workflow.json rather than the primary checkout's — so a session on the base branch may drive a worktree that stands on a feature branch, and a session on a feature branch may not drive a checkout that stands on the base. It fails CLOSED on the five forms where the branch it can see is not the branch the write would land on: a line that both changes branch (switch, checkout, branch -f) and writes; a repository-selecting path it cannot recover, including two different quoted paths for one flag anywhere on the line, since recovery is line-global and cannot tell whose span is whose; a git segment carrying a write token alongside a global option this guard does not know, which is named in the refusal; a git segment carrying a write token whose subcommand it cannot establish otherwise; and a shell wrapper whose payload it cannot read on a line that carries a write token.
